last_report.message: Wrote test_cases.json with six cases covering nested object merge, null removal and absent-key no-op, list replacement, boolean/number type mismatch (ValueError), non-object base rejection (ValueError), and key ordering. Expected values follow the user contract. module.py was not modified.

content.assignment: Write test_cases.json only. It must be a JSON list of at least four distinct cases for solve(data) implementing the deep-merge contract. Each case has an input object with keys base and patch, plus exactly one of output (expected JSON result) or error (exception class name, e.g. ValueError). Optional name/notes fields are allowed. Cover: nested object merge (base {a:{x:1}}, patch {a:{y:2}} gives {a:{x:1,y:2}}); null removes a key and removing an absent key is a no-op; list replacement with no concatenation; boolean vs number type mismatch raises ValueError; non-object base or patch raises ValueError; key order (base order first, then patch-only keys in patch order). Expected values must follow the user contract exactly, not the current module.py behavior. Do not write module.py.
content.user_contract: Implement solve(data) for {"base": object, "patch": object}. Both must be JSON objects; otherwise raise ValueError. Produce the deep merge of patch into base. For each key in patch: if the value is null, remove that key from the result, and removing a key that is absent is a no-op; if both the base value and the patch value are objects, merge them recursively by the same rules; if both are lists, the patch list replaces the base list entirely with no concatenation; if the base key is absent, the patch value is inserted as is; otherwise, when the two values are of different JSON types, raise ValueError. Two values count as the same type when both are objects, both are lists, both are strings, both are booleans, or both are numbers; booleans and numbers are different types. Key order in the result is: the keys of base in their original order, then the keys found only in patch in their order of appearance in patch. Do not mutate either input.

artifact_contracts.test_cases.json: JSON list of at least four distinct test inputs. Each case has input plus exactly one of output (the expected JSON result) or error (exception class name). Descriptive extra fields such as name or notes are allowed and ignored by execution. Test expectations must match the user contract.

content.receipt_terms: A pass review requires a genuine successful test receipt bound to the delivered module.py and test_cases.json versions. Receipts are returned to the session that ran the tests; there is no tool for retrieving a receipt issued by another session.
